lessons: My WR went 1-2 with only two fliers, Abbey Griffin and Spectral Rider, and both losses ran 17 to 24 turns, so draft a third flier or Rally the Peasants over late ground filler.
Tonight contradicted the cheap-creature plan: my curve won 2-0 in 12 turns against WU, but BG and UB ground me out in 17- and 24-turn losses, so cheap bodies need late fliers.
Keep a flexible late threat even at the cost of a cheap Thraben Sentry, since my WR had none and lost both of its long games.
Count fliers before committing: my black-green deck, with Corpse Lunge, Dead Weight and Tribute to Hunger, went 0-2 against a white-blue deck with Stitched Drake and Angel of Flight Alabaster.
Value recursion over filler: Round 2's 37-turn game was a grind, so Unburial Rites, which I cut for a 23rd spell, may deserve a slot over a weak body.
Check which colour is open before committing: seat 5's white-green went 3-0 while my black-green deck finished 1-2, so reassess the flow after pack 1.
Early picks Brimstone Volley, Darkthicket Wolf, Prey Upon and Riot Devils were wasted off-colour; commit to WU by pick five and take blue and white removal over speculative cards.
The guide calls Wooden Stakes skip-worthy, yet the BR deck that beat me 2-1 registered two, so cheap ground-stopping cards matter when your fliers can't block early.
Round 2's WR humans beat my Moon Heron and Stitched Drake deck 0-2 in 12 turns, so the guide's 'fliers win' line needs a lower curve of two- and three-drops.
Red was the open lane tonight: pack 2's first picks Galvanic Juggernaut and Into the Maw of Hell fed a 2-1 BR deck, so take red removal like Brimstone Volley early.
Don't main two Wooden Stake without reads: they were dead against Round 3's WG deck, which was mostly Humans and Spirits (Fiend Hunter, Slayer of the Wicked), and I lost 0-2 to it.
Tonight's WG went 0-3 with Avacyn's Pilgrim and Thraben Sentry, contradicting the guide's 2-1 WG claim: our ground bodies lost to Chapel Geist, Moon Heron and Stitched Drake in 20-to-34-turn games.
Claustrophobia taken first was stranded in WG; early removal needs a pair decision by pick 5, as the guide says, before it outranks on-colour creatures.
Our WG had only Orchard Spirit and two Somberwald Spiders against WU's fliers, so take a third evasive finisher in pack 3 over a fourth ground two-drop.
Take Fiend Hunter and Bonds of Faith early: with Spidery Grasp, that removal and the creature base went 6-0 in games across three opponents, including the WG deck that went 0-3.
Expect long games: all six games ran 20 to 34 turns, so late-game value like Gavony Township, Mentor of the Meek and Grizzled Outcasts earned its place in the deck.
My picks include neither Fiend Hunter nor Slayer of the Wicked, yet the WG deck that beat me 2-0 ran both; take white removal creatures over filler.
The guide's warning against mill-yourself cards outside UG was contradicted: my UB deck with Armored Skaab won two of three matches, 4-2 in games.
Pack 2 spent two picks on Manor Skeleton and one on Lost in the Mist, all cut before build; take playable creatures or removal over those.
Garruk Relentless, my pack 3 first pick, never made my blue-white deck, so settle on two colours before chasing off-colour bombs like it.
Blue was the deepest colour: the blue-white build around Stitched Drake, Forbidden Alchemy and Armored Skaab went 2-1 in matches, so take blue depth early and cut the hedges.
My round 1 loss was 0-2 to a UB deck with Murder of Crows and Moon Heron in 16- and 24-turn games, so prioritise cheap flyer defence like Abbey Griffin and Angel of Flight Alabaster.
